# Nedaa | نداء

> Free, open-source, privacy-first prayer-times, Quran-reader and Islamic-companion app for iOS and Android. No data collection. No selling. No ads. No accounts. No paywalls. No premium tier.

Nedaa (Arabic: نداء, "the call" — a reference to the Adhan) is built around accurate prayer times, real OS-level Fajr alarms, a Quran reader carrying three Madinah Mushaf editions with word-level read-along recitation, daily Athkar from the Hisn al-Muslim dataset, Qibla, Hijri tools, an Umrah guide, and a Qada (fasting) tracker. It ships on iOS, Google Play (Android with GMS), and Huawei AppGallery (Android with HMS — a deliberately maintained build for Huawei devices without Google Mobile Services).

The app is open source at https://github.com/NedaaDevs/nedaa under [its license](https://github.com/NedaaDevs/nedaa/blob/master/LICENSE). The Tanzil Quran text used in the Quran reader is separately licensed under CC-BY 3.0; attribution is preserved in the app's in-app Acknowledgements screen.

## Pillar feature pages

- [Prayer times](https://nedaa.dev/docs/prayer-times): 23 calculation methods plus a fully custom option (Muslim World League, ISNA, Umm al-Qura, Karachi, Egyptian, Diyanet, JAKIM, Kemenag, Singapore MUIS, and more); provider-abstracted at the API layer with Aladhan as the currently-implemented upstream; both Hanafi and standard Asr juristic schools; high-latitude adjustment; works offline after first sync.
- [Prayer alarm](https://nedaa.dev/docs/prayer-alarm): real OS-level prayer alarms (Fajr, Jummah, and custom types) — Apple AlarmKit on iOS 26+ (alarm feature requires iOS 26; not available on earlier iOS), native Android foreground alarm service. Optional wake-up challenges (tap or math). Custom Athan sound per alarm type. Bypasses Do Not Disturb.
- [Athkar](https://nedaa.dev/docs/athkar): morning, evening, and occasion-based supplications from the Hisn al-Muslim dataset (Sa'id ibn Ali ibn Wahaf al-Qahtani). Multiple reciter audio voices. Focus-mode reader. Custom user-added athkar. Gentle (non-gamified) habit tracking with pause/resume.
- [Qada fasting tracker](https://nedaa.dev/docs/qada-tracker): counts down missed Ramadan fasts with a Ramadan-anchored reminder for the canonical "make up before next Ramadan" deadline. Privacy-mode hide. For fasting qada only — does not track missed prayers.
- [Quran reader](https://nedaa.dev/docs/quran-reader): three Madinah Mushaf editions from the King Fahd Glorious Qur'an Printing Complex — 1405 (QCF v1), 1420 (QCF v2), 1439 (QCF v4 with tajweed colour) — on the standard 604-page layout, plus a text mode that needs no edition download at all, rendering the Tanzil Uthmani text at 20–48pt. Read-along recitation highlighting the whole verse or the individual word, in Murattal/Mujawwad/Tajweed styles, with per-surah offline audio download. A separate Listen surface carries the sleep timer, the continue/repeat/stop choice at the end of a surah, and whole-reciter download. Bookmarks, highlights with user-named colours, mutashabihat (similar-verse) comparison with user memory aids, and a built-in reference for tajweed colours, waqf stop signs, and prostration verses. Optional Friday Surah Al-Kahf reminder. Offline once downloaded.

## Comparison and research

- [How Islamic prayer-time apps differ on privacy, ads, and openness](https://nedaa.dev/docs/comparison-privacy-ads-openness): category-level comparison framework — four dimensions (data collection, advertising, pricing, source transparency) with "questions to ask of any app you're considering." Brand-voice safe; no head-to-head.
- [Why digital Quran apps look the way they do](https://nedaa.dev/docs/islamic-typography) ([AR](https://nedaa.dev/ar/docs/islamic-typography)): a guide to Islamic typography on small screens — why mushaf pages ship as images rather than rendered text, the Uthmani vs Imlaei rasm question, hybrid rendering with a per-edition glyph-bounds database, diacritic-insensitive FTS5 search, and Arabic/Latin typeface pairing. Written from inside the codebase.

## Upstream data sources

- [Aladhan API](https://aladhan.com): currently-implemented prayer-time calculation upstream. All 23 calculation methods Nedaa exposes today come from Aladhan. Nedaa's prayer-time computation is provider-abstracted at the API layer; the architecture supports adding additional providers without app updates.
- [Tanzil Project](https://tanzil.net): Quran text in Uthmani script, CC-BY 3.0. Attribution to "Tanzil Project" preserved in Nedaa's in-app Acknowledgements screen as required by the license.
- [QuranicAudio](https://quranicaudio.com) and [quran.com](https://quran.com): Quran reciter audio, mirrored via QUL. Credited in Nedaa's in-app Acknowledgements screen.
- [Quranic Universal Library (QUL)](https://qul.tarteel.ai) by Tarteel: verse divisions and recitation word-timing used by the Quran reader's read-along.
- King Fahd Glorious Qur'an Printing Complex (KFGQPC), Madinah: the UthmanicHafs font and the Madinah Mushaf page layout, shipped as the QCF v1 / v2 / v4 page-image editions.
- Hisn al-Muslim by Sa'id ibn Ali ibn Wahaf al-Qahtani: source dataset for athkar.

## Distribution

- iOS App Store: bundle id `dev.nedaa.app`.
- Google Play (Android, GMS): package `dev.nedaa.android`.
- Huawei AppGallery (Android, HMS): same package, separate `production-hms` build with no Google Mobile Services dependencies.
- Source: https://github.com/NedaaDevs/nedaa
- Translation: https://crowdin.com/project/nedaa-v2 (English, Arabic, Malay, Urdu currently shipped; RTL-first design).
- Support: support@nedaa.dev

## Optional

- [Developer guide](https://github.com/NedaaDevs/nedaa/blob/master/docs/DEV-README.md): codebase orientation, build setup (including GMS vs HMS Android variants), native module overview, contribution conventions.
